text: This is where Seoa is calling from: a stampede under the market roof, and eyeless hounds bounding in.
She's hauling a crying boy into a rice-cake shop, briefing her brother like a dispatcher.
Two market grannies take orders from a fifteen-year-old, and a dozen people vanish into the back.
Just in time. A hound hits the shutter and dents it in the shape of its head.
Back against the metal, she routes him in like he would: down an alley too narrow for a pack.
Jaeha runs flat out, still bloody from the tower, against the fleeing crowd.
He begs her to climb somewhere high. She refuses: somebody has to empty the fish lane.
The fear hardens. He knows his sister. To keep her safe, he'll have to keep up.
At the pharmacy alley, a Gate Rescue van mounts the kerb.
Out jumps Choi of the Gate Rescue Corps. He's starting to expect Jaeha at every disaster.
Then the grin goes. Help is a quarter of an hour out, and the guild that locked Jaeha in sat on this contract twice.
Some luck: gate mana leaks into the street, so summons recover in a minute, not four hours.
Yesterday he wanted no cameras. Now phones film from every side, and he shuts the notebook anyway. Nib approves.
Nib goes first, on a five-minute clock. Borro waits his turn.
Nib cuts a leaping hound in half in mid-air.
Bomi arrives breathless, her drone already climbing. He needs a map before he moves anyone.
From above: alleys like ribs, packs of hounds, and a footbridge at the market's edge.
Seoa names the problem: her people have one way out, and it's over that bridge.
Seoa's alley gave him the idea: every lane funnels into one tiny square, where a giant meets them single file.
Through the link, he hands out the jobs: one wall, one sheepdog.
Borro takes the square on his own five-minute clock, and his shield plugs the alley.
Single file, exactly as planned, and each one meets the iron alone.
Every hit lands in Jaeha too: Carry gives him a quarter of Borro's damage.
The sheepdog works from above, dropping off the awnings onto any hound that strays.
One slips past toward the hidden children. The kimchi granny steps out with a giant radish.
Full swing, perfect follow-through. The radish snaps, and the hound goes down among the tubs.
Nib drops from above and finishes the dazed hound with one knife.
Nib gives her a soldier's nod, one veteran to another. She has more where that came from.
Seoa runs the household budget, so of course she's counting: fourteen heads, hand in hand.
Yerin, who froze on her first raid, talks herself through healing a bitten leg. Choi carries an old woman past.
Two hounds hit Borro from two alleys at once: one takes the shield, one his shell.
Two summons, two loads. Jaeha's nose bleeds again, and the load climbs to ninety percent.
Forty-eight thousand are watching Bomi's stream, and the husk story is already falling apart.
Under the fish lane, violet light and heat pour up the stairwell. The ice is melting.
Then a second wave boils out of the gate, twenty hounds or more.
And they're heading for the footbridge, where Seoa's line has just started to climb.
The square was a good plan, and it's over. Both summons fall back to the bridge.
Borro ploughs down the main street like a battering ram, Nib running the awnings above.
Seoa's people are halfway across the footbridge, and the flood is right behind them.
The last time Nib held a gate alone, nobody came back for him. He takes the top step anyway.
The stairs fit two hounds at a time, and Nib cuts down every pair.
Then the road under the bridge bulges up, steaming and glowing violet.
A crack races up the bridge's only pier.
The deck sags. People scream and grab the railings, and Seoa holds a child tight.
Jaeha staggers out, sees his sister on a sagging bridge, and has time for one order.
Borro leaps onto the buckling road and runs underneath.
The pier gives way, and Borro catches the bridge on his shell, fourteen people above him.
A share of that bridge lands on Jaeha. A hundred and sixty percent, and this time it isn't a warning.
Through the pain, a strange thought: a stoneback carrier, doing exactly what his name says.
Walking backwards with a child on her hip, Seoa keeps fourteen people calm on a tilting deck.
Fifty seconds left, sweat running under the mask, and still the giant won't hurry anyone.
Nib's clock runs out first. His outline flickers with eight seconds left.
It ends just as a hound leaps. In rest form, he can't fight for a whole minute.
The hound flattens him. He holds its jaws off with his one remaining knife.
In tears, Bomi makes the streamer's ultimate sacrifice: she flies her drone straight at the hound.
The drone explodes against the hound and knocks it off Nib, down the stairs.
The stream dies with nearly fifty-two thousand watching. The chat mourns the drone.
The hounds come again, and Nib stands in their way anyway: one knife, no glow.
Then Choi blasts an extinguisher, and the kimchi granny, true to her word, brings another radish.
Twelve seconds, bought. Jaeha raises a bloody hand, and Nib gets five more minutes.
Nib's eye flares amber, and he tears out of the white cloud, bursting hounds into ash.
Seoa steps off with the last child. Two seconds left, and Borro waits for her count.
Only then does Borro step out, and the footbridge crashes down behind him, empty.
The dust settles. Across the gap, Seoa stands in front of her fourteen.
Dusty, crying and grinning, she holds up the one thing she never let go of.
Jaeha laughs in spite of himself. Borro's welcome dinner survived.
But the steam from the road is getting thicker, and the cracks glow violet.
Choi is sweating through his jacket in autumn. That heat is coming from somewhere.
The laugh dies on Jaeha's face. The break isn't finished.
The road under the wreck swells into a dome, and Borro gets five fresh minutes.
And the break's boss bursts out of the street: a jade-and-gold serpent, horned and hooded, three storeys high.
A C-grade break boss, a grade above the alpha that left him bleeding today. The crack on its brow leaks violet.
